answer: Because the inlet audit recomputes usage from the jade history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. Each identity declares a compute budget of 551 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. A farm running 105 keys thus pays for 105 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the gale declaration. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
